titulo: Making it to the end of the month
intro: Money at home and in the region: wages, prices, loans and change.
p.economía.consejo: It has an accent on the í: «e-ko-no-MI-a». Someone who studies it is «el economista».
p.sueldo.consejo: It is almost the same as «el salario»; in conversation you hear «sueldo» a lot.
p.gastos.consejo: It is almost always plural: «los gastos de la casa». The opposite is «los ingresos».
p.alquiler.consejo: It is masculine: «el alquiler». From the verb «alquilar», used for flats and cars.
p.ahorros.consejo: The h is silent: «a-O-rros». It is almost always used in the plural.
p.préstamo.consejo: It has an accent on the é: «PRES-ta-mo». With a loan you pay interest.
p.intereses.consejo: In the singular, «el interés» is also what catches your attention.
p.precios.consejo: In the singular it is «el precio». Prices can «subir» or «bajar».
p.cosecha.consejo: The «ch» sounds like in «chocolate». A good harvest gives a lot of fruit.
p.exportar.consejo: It has «ex-», meaning to take outwards. The opposite is «importar».
p.importar.consejo: It has another very common meaning: «no me importa» means «I do not mind».
p.turismo.consejo: It comes from «turista». On many coasts it gives work to many people.
p.llegar a fin de mes.consejo: It is almost always used in the negative: «no llego a fin de mes».
b1.texto:
At home you earn a **sueldo** and you pay **gastos**: the **alquiler**, the bills, the food.

- If you put money aside, you have **ahorros**.
- If it is not enough, you ask for a **préstamo** and pay **intereses**.
- If money runs short, you do not **llegas a fin de mes**.

In the **economía** of a place, **precios** go up or down. A country **exporta** what it sells abroad and **importa** what it buys abroad. From the countryside comes the **cosecha**; from the coasts, **turismo**.

To describe a change: **cada vez más**, **cada vez menos**, **ha subido un cinco por ciento**.
b2.titulo: Sums at the end of the month
b2.f0.texto: How are you managing until the end of the month?
b2.f2.texto: Prices have gone up five per cent.
b2.f3.texto: The rent costs me half of my salary.
b2.f4.texto: I have a loan and I pay a lot of interest.
b2.f7.texto: I hope wages go up soon.
b4.titulo: More and more, less and less
b4.texto:
To describe how something changes, use these formulas:

- **cada vez más** + adjective or noun: **cada vez más caro**.
- **cada vez menos** + noun: **cada vez menos ahorros**.
- **subir, bajar, aumentar, disminuir** + **un** + number + **por ciento**: **han subido un cinco por ciento**.

Note: **cada vez más** never changes, but the adjective does: **los precios son cada vez más altos**.

For changes that reach up to today, use the present perfect: **han subido, ha bajado**.
b4.e0.texto: It is harder and harder to make ends meet.
b4.e1.texto: There are fewer and fewer tourists on the coast.
b5.f0.texto: At dawn, the boats reach the harbour with the fish still alive.
b5.f1.texto: On the ice the sardines and the octopuses shine.
b5.f2.texto: A woman arranges boxes of fruit under a striped awning.
b5.f3.texto: The smell of the sea mixes with that of the oranges.
b5.f4.texto: The sellers shout the prices in hoarse voices.
b5.f5.texto: Years ago almost everyone lived from the sea and from the harvest.
b5.f6.texto: Today tourism gives work to many people.
b5.f7.texto: In summer the hotels fill up with tired and happy travellers.
b5.f8.texto: In winter many families count every euro with worry.
b5.f9.texto: An old fisherman looks at the sea and dreams of a better salary.
b6.o0.refuerzo: It is not about travel, but about money.
b6.o1: tener dinero para todo el mes
b6.o1.refuerzo: That's it! The money has to last until the last day.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Earning more helps, but the expression is about whether it is enough.
b6.pregunta: What does «llegar a fin de mes» mean?
b7.frase: Los precios han subido un cinco ____ ciento.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Well done! The fixed expression is «por ciento».
b7.o1.refuerzo: «De ciento» does not exist here; you say «por ciento».
b7.o2.refuerzo: «En ciento» is not said. The expression is «por ciento».
b7.pregunta: Prices are going up. Which word is missing?
b8.frase: Cada vez cuesta más llegar a fin de mes
b8.traduccion: It is harder and harder to make ends meet
b9.o0.refuerzo: To import is to buy from abroad, exactly the opposite.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Deber» is to owe. Here it sells.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes! To export is to sell to another country.
b9.pregunta: A country sells wine abroad. What does it do?
b10.frase: Pedí un ____ al banco y pago intereses.
b10.o0.refuerzo: The company pays the salary, not the bank.
b10.o2.refuerzo: A price is not asked of a bank and produces no interest.
b10.pregunta: You pay interest to the bank. What did you ask for?
b12.o0: Todo es cada vez más caro.
b12.o0.refuerzo: That's it! «Cada vez más» shows that the price rises.
b12.o1: Todo es cada vez menos caro.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Menos caro» means the price goes down.
b12.o2: Todo es siempre igual de caro.
b12.pregunta: Which sentence says that life gets more expensive?
p.llegas.consejo: From «llegar». The «ll» sounds like «y»: «YE-gas». Before «e» it is written «gu»: «llegue».
p.suban.consejo: Subjunctive of «subir»: «suba, subas, suba, subamos, suban». Here it comes after «ojalá».
p.sueldos.consejo: Plural of «sueldo». The «ue» is one sound: «SWEL-dos», two syllables.
p.barcas.consejo: Plural of «barca». The «c» before «a» sounds like k: «BAR-kas».
p.puerto.consejo: The «ue» is one sound: «PWER-to», two syllables. A port can be for boats or for computers.
p.sardinas.consejo: It looks and sounds almost like English «sardines», with the stress on «DI».
p.pulpos.consejo: Plural of «pulpo». An octopus has eight arms. The «p» is pronounced twice, in «pul» and «pos».
p.toldo.consejo: A «toldo» is made of cloth and stretches over a stall or a terrace.
p.mezcla.consejo: From «mezclar». The «z» sounds like «th»: «METH-kla». With «se», it mixes by itself.
p.vendedores.consejo: Plural of «vendedor». The stress falls on «DO»: «ben-de-DO-res».
p.voces.consejo: Plural of «voz»: the «z» becomes «c» in the plural. The «v» sounds like b.
p.roncas.consejo: From «ronco»: «ronco, ronca, roncos, roncas». It starts with a strong «rr»: «RRON-kas».
p.vivían.consejo: Imperfect of «vivir». The accent on the «í» keeps «i» and «a» in separate syllables: «bi-BI-an».
p.hoteles.consejo: The «h» is silent: «o-TE-les». The plural is «hoteles», not «hotels».
p.cansados.consejo: From «cansado»: «cansado, cansada, cansados, cansadas». It agrees with «viajeros».
p.felices.consejo: Plural of «feliz»: the «z» becomes «c» in «felices». It is the same for masculine and feminine.
p.familias.consejo: Plural of «familia». The «ia» is one syllable at the end: «fa-MI-lyas».
p.cuentan.consejo: From «contar». The «o» changes to «ue» when stressed: «cuento, cuentas, cuenta, cuentan».
p.euro.consejo: The «eu» is one sound: «EW-ro». The plural is «euros».
p.preocupación.consejo: It ends in «-ción» and the stress falls on «THYON». The verb is «preocuparse».
p.pescador.consejo: For a woman: «la pescadora». It comes from «pescar». The «sc» is two sounds: «pes-ka».
p.vino.consejo: The «v» sounds like b: «BI-no». It is made from grapes.
p.pedí.consejo: Past of «pedir». It has an accent on the «í» and the stress falls on it: «pe-DI».
